_note: Thomas, 2026-09-06: 'the rest of the uk/GB/ireland/scotland' — the devolved half of thin-coverage round 2. The corpus held nothing at all for Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland's own statistical outputs: everything British was either England-only local government finance or UK-wide ONS. This round mints the devolved core in all three and, more importantly, wires it to the UK-wide releases it visibly depends on — GERS to ONS public sector finances, the NI Composite Economic Index to the Blue Book and the LFS, the NI and Welsh labour market series to the UK LFS, and four separate Code of Practice for Statistics ties. Every url and every evidence_url was raw-verified HTTP 200 before use; gov.scot, nrscotland.gov.uk, nisra.gov.uk, datavis.nisra.gov.uk, gov.wales, scotlandscensus.gov.uk and fiscalcommission.scot all answered a browser-UA curl and nothing was blocked. Two nodes carried A-grade evidence to artefacts that did not exist yet — HM Treasury PESA/CRA and ONS Country and regional public sector finances — and are minted in the companion slice gb-national-fill-2026-09-06.

reports.title: Government Expenditure and Revenue Scotland
reports.publisher: Scottish Government (Office of the Chief Economic Adviser)
reports.description: Accredited official statistics estimating the revenue raised in Scotland and the cost of the public services provided for Scotland; the 2024-25 edition is the thirty-second in the series. Revenue is constrained to UK outturn from ONS public sector finances and apportioned to Scotland stream by stream; expenditure uses Scottish Government accounting data together with HM Treasury's Public Expenditure Statistical Analyses and its Country and regional analysis.

reports.title: GDP Quarterly National Accounts, Scotland
reports.description: Scotland's quarterly national accounts: GDP by the output, income and expenditure approaches, household sector income and expenditure accounts, and quarterly public sector revenue. The published methodology states that a full set of national accounts comparable with ONS UK output is neither practical nor conceptually possible for Scotland, so QNAS produces a defined subset, mixing top-down Scottish shares of UK results with bottom-up Scottish sources.

reports.title: Scotland's Census 2022
reports.description: The decennial census of the Scottish population, taken on 20 March 2022 after being moved from 2021 because of COVID-19. The Registrar General for Scotland takes the census under the Census Act 1920, with each census requiring a further Census Order and Census Regulations; the Census (Scotland) Order 2020 and Regulations 2020 governed this one. First results were published in September 2023 and the statistics were designated accredited official statistics.
reports.cadence_note: Decennial. Scotland's Census 2022 was taken on 20 March 2022, a year later than the rest of the UK because of COVID-19.

reports.title: Mid-year population estimates, Scotland
reports.description: Annual accredited official statistics estimating the usually resident population of Scotland at 30 June each year, by age and sex. The census provides the base population, which is rolled forward each year for births, deaths, net migration and other changes such as armed forces and prison populations. NRS rebased the 2011-2022 series in June 2024 following Scotland's Census 2022 and revised it again in January 2025.

reports.title: Scotland's Economic and Fiscal Forecasts
reports.description: The Scottish Fiscal Commission's official forecasts of the Scottish economy and of devolved tax revenues and social security spending, published alongside the Scottish Budget. The Commission states it does not produce official statistics but voluntarily applies the UK Statistics Authority's Code of Practice for Statistics, and its forecast comparison tables set its figures against the OBR, NIESR, the Bank of England and HM Treasury.

reports.title: Census 2021, Northern Ireland
reports.publisher: Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency (NISRA)
reports.description: The 2021 census of population and households in Northern Ireland, conducted by NISRA; first population and household estimates were published on 24 May 2022. The census results are the benchmark to which Northern Ireland's population statistics are anchored and from which subsequent mid-year estimates are rolled forward.
reports.cadence_note: Decennial. Census day for the 2021 Northern Ireland census was 21 March 2021.

reports.title: Mid-Year Population Estimates for Northern Ireland
reports.publisher: Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency (NISRA)
reports.description: Annual accredited official statistics estimating the usually resident population of Northern Ireland at 30 June each year, produced by the cohort component method. Births and deaths come from General Register Office registrations; migration inflows and outflows are estimated from the Medical Card Register, with flows to Great Britain constrained to figures agreed between NISRA, ONS and National Records of Scotland.

reports.title: Northern Ireland Composite Economic Index
reports.publisher: Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency (NISRA)
reports.description: A quarterly measure of economic activity in Northern Ireland, broadly equivalent to the output measure of GDP produced by ONS. It combines the NI Index of Services, Index of Production, Quarterly Construction Enquiry, Quarterly Employment Survey public sector jobs and unpublished agricultural output, weighted using ONS regional balanced GVA by industry and aggregated by annual chain-linking, with self-employment estimates drawn from the Labour Force Survey.

reports.title: Northern Ireland Labour Force Survey
reports.publisher: Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency (NISRA)
reports.description: A survey of households at private addresses in Northern Ireland providing the information used to develop, manage and evaluate NI labour market policy. It is the Northern Ireland component of the UK Labour Force Survey, managed by NISRA's Central Survey Unit while ONS Social Surveys manages the GB component, and it applies standard International Labour Organisation definitions of economic status. It is the largest social survey in Northern Ireland.

reports.title: Labour market overview, Wales
reports.description: A monthly Welsh Government release summarising the latest statistics on the Welsh labour market, drawing on HMRC Pay As You Earn Real Time Information and the Labour Force Survey. It reports headline employment, unemployment and economic inactivity rates for Wales alongside payrolled employment and earnings, with Welsh Government commentary on LFS data quality.

reports.title: Mid year estimates of the population, Wales
reports.description: An annual Welsh Government statistical bulletin presenting the ONS mid-year population estimates for Wales by local authority, age and sex. The underlying estimates are produced by ONS to methods set out in the ONS England and Wales methods guide; Welsh Government statisticians quality-assure the Welsh figures before publication. The bulletin notes that statistical uncertainty is lowest immediately after a census and grows as estimates are rolled forward.

dependencies.basis: RESEARCHED 2026-09-06 (GB devolved core round), MINTED 2026-09-06 after Thomas ruled that a methodology table cell naming a source is caption-equivalent. The GERS 2024-25 detailed revenue methodology names the Living Costs and Food Survey as the apportionment source for tobacco duties, insurance premium tax, betting and gaming duties, the horserace betting levy, the soft drinks levy and the National Lottery contribution — every one of those inside a methodology table cell, none in prose, which is why it was refused when this slice was first written. Graded B, the grade the ruling assigns to caption-shaped evidence. Read live from the cited URL (HTTP 200), quote verbatim. || REGRADED B -> A 2026-09-06 evening on Thomas's caption ruling. PLAYBOOK-CORPUS §7a's table-cell clause said a methodology table cell is 'caption-equivalent' and then graded it B, while the chart-caption ruling it extends grades a caption A. Thomas resolved the contradiction in favour of A ('i think the caption sourcing is ok and both can be A's. we need to fix that line for consistency'), and caption-equivalent means equivalent, so this moves with it. His caveat applies and is met here: what carries the citation is the disclosure itself, and this table's entire stated purpose is to tell subscribers which methodology each data category must follow.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Method as for betting and gaming duty – using Scotland’s proportion of estimated UK spend on betting etc as estimated by the Living Costs and Food Survey.

_dropped.why: RESOLVED 2026-09-06. This entry recorded the edge as no-document because every mention of the Living Costs and Food Survey in the GERS revenue methodology sits in a methodology table cell rather than in prose — six of them, covering tobacco duties, insurance premium tax, betting and gaming duties, the horserace betting levy, the soft drinks levy and the National Lottery contribution. Thomas ruled the same day that a methodology table cell naming a source IS caption-equivalent, extending the 2026-08-30 chart-caption ruling: a table whose purpose is to disclose sources discloses them. The edge is now live at B. A corpus-wide sweep of _dropped entries refused on this shape found exactly one other candidate, the Welsh Index of Multiple Deprivation, which is blocked for a different reason (its source tables cite the 2011 Census, which has no node). The ruling does NOT reopen agency-only table entries: on-ompf's Appendix F attributes five measures to 'Statistics Canada' with no publication named, and that stays refused — the cell has to name the artefact.

_dropped.edge: sct-census-2022 -> Census Act 1920 / Census (Scotland) Order 2020 (no node minted)
_dropped.why: LEAD 2026-09-06. The Scotland's Census 2022 General Report states 'The Registrar General for Scotland takes a census in Scotland under the Census Act 1920' and describes the Census (Scotland) Order 2020 and Regulations 2020. Clean legal_basis evidence for a statutory spine the corpus does not yet carry: the UK's census legislation is entirely absent, in contrast to Australia's Census and Statistics Act 1905 which this round minted. Worth a round of its own alongside the England and Wales Census Act 1920 instruments.

The January 2026 forecast states 'Given the ongoing concerns with the quality of the official labour market statistics from the Labour Force Survey and the Annual Population Survey, our view of employment growth and the unemployment rate is based on a range of indicators including Real Time Information payroll data.' A named non-use is not a dependency; minting this would misrepresent the source.

_dropped.edge: Welsh Index of Multiple Deprivation (no node minted)
_dropped.why: LEAD 2026-09-06. The WIMD 2019 Technical Report was read in full. Every source attribution ('Source: 2011 Census, Office for National Statistics'; 'Denominator: Small Area Population Estimates, 2018, ONS') sits in per-indicator source and denominator tables and never in body text, and the census cited is the 2011 Census, which has no corpus node. The node was not minted because it would have arrived with no defensible edge. Wales is the weakest of the three devolved administrations for this project's purposes: its releases mostly republish and quality-assure ONS output rather than documenting their own derivation chains.

NOT FOUND 2026-09-06. The GERS preface, About page and both methodology chapters name ONS Public Sector Finances, ONS Country and regional public sector finances and QNAS, but never the Blue Book or the UK National Accounts by title. The three edges those documents DO support were minted.
